success_patterns: Every success identified the plain natural-theorem option (the hub) and checked each other option as 'hub + one delta' or 'hub with one swap'. The deltas were: a dropped hypothesis ('even without the flatness / weight-type assumption'), an endpoint or range shift ('one may take λ=μ', 'α=min{s,1-s}'), a sharper constant ('6g-6' instead of '6g'), a shaved log or exact asymptotic constant (loglog n, ~K√n log n), and a changed constant dependence ('independent of s').

The winner sat at the pivot of the strength ladder between 'true but weaker' and 'sharper but unproved'. Examples: weak mixing, which beats ergodic but not strongly mixing or 'uniquely ergodic but not weakly mixing'; at most 6g multi-graftings, which beats 'finitely many' but not 6g-6; O(√n log n), which beats n^{1/2+o(1)} but not O(√n loglog n).

The winner stated every part of the natural theorem and kept every stem hypothesis. It included existence AND uniqueness, and the subcritical case AND the critical case. Existence-only options and a singular-behaviour-only option were the truncations that lost.

Riders that add a new object or structure were rejected. Examples: 'totally geodesic', 'decorated tree', 'supercritical only at...', 'always critical for every u>0', 'finite index in a hyperbolic 3-manifold group'. Several fail against the stem's own definitions: a thin subgroup is Zariski dense, so it cannot come from a totally geodesic surface, and a branching law cannot be both 'subcritical for u<u_C' and 'always critical'.

For regularity estimates the winner used the local norm named in the stem and the natural exponent. It rejected exponents above the boundary-regularity threshold (2s-ε > s), a weakened 'some α' exponent, a global-norm replacement, and a dropped parameter dependence.

For long enumerated 'which items hold / fail' options, the options were compared by their set differences. Only the differing items were decided, by a small test case. The option listing both the holding and the failing items correctly beat the truncated 'hold only' option.

patch.reasoning: The core workflow already captures most of these successes: the hub, the strength ladder pivot, and rejecting 'even without', sharper constants and riders. The previous long checklist edit was rejected, so the new content is kept to two short bullets. One covers a recurring option format that is not explicit: lists of items that hold or fail, decided through their symmetric difference. The other makes 'test every rider against the stem's own definitions' an executable step. Both sit at checklist level and flip no currently correct behaviour.

edits.target: ## Near-duplicate options: constants, quantifiers, ranges, exact details
edits.content: - List or membership options (each option enumerates which items hold and which fail): write the symmetric difference of the lists, mark every item that appears in some options but not others, and decide ONLY those items by a small test (smallest graph or case, a regular or degenerate input, homogeneity). Pick the option whose differing items all pass. If one option lists the holding items correctly but omits the 'the rest fail' clause, it is the truncated version of the full classification and loses to it only when the full classification's differing items are verified.

edits.target: ## Tie-breaker: signature of the winning option
edits.content: - Rider-vs-definition check: test every extra descriptor in an option against the stem's own defined terms and against the option's other clauses. A rider that contradicts a stem definition (e.g. 'thin' means Zariski dense and infinite index, yet the option forces a totally geodesic origin) or that makes another clause of the same option vacuous or contradictory (a 'subcritical for u<u_C' clause together with 'always critical for every u') is false. Discard it before any strength ranking.
